findings.claim: The requirement says MessagePack attributes on T must be honoured if present. GeneratedFormatterCollector never reads T's attributes. Without a surrogate, CreateContractlessMembers serializes every public readable member, even when T marks it [IgnoreMember] or [IgnoreDataMember]. [MessagePackObject], [Key] and [DataContract]/[DataMember(Name=...)] on T are ignored as well, so the wire format differs from what T declares. [DataContract]/[DataMember] is the realistic case: Project A can use it without referencing MessagePack.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterLogicReceipts.IgnoredMemberOnFormattedTypeIsNotSerialized(IgnoreMember / IgnoreDataMember): runs the generator on a public property marked ignored and asserts the user-declared formatter source does not mention it. It fails on head because 'Secret' is emitted.

findings.claim: IsPartial checks only the formatter's own declaration. If the formatter is nested in a containing type that is not partial, no MsgPack019 is reported. The template (EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces over Info.Formatter's containers) then re-declares the outer type as partial, which yields a CS0260 compile error in generated code instead of a MessagePack diagnostic.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterLogicReceipts.FormatterNestedInNonPartialTypeIsDiagnosedOrCompiles: asserts that either MsgPack019 is reported or the output compilation has no CS0260. It fails on head.

findings.claim: The ForAttributeWithMetadataName predicate accepts only ClassDeclarationSyntax. A `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial record F : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;` matches neither this pipeline nor the diagnostics pipeline. It gets no implementation and no MsgPack019/020 diagnostic, so the user sees only CS0535 for the missing members.

receipt_plan.detail: MessagePackGenerator.cs:31 predicate `node is ClassDeclarationSyntax`: a RecordDeclarationSyntax target is filtered out before GeneratedFormatterCollector can report anything.

findings.claim: GetInstanceMembers keeps the first member seen per name, walking from the most-derived type, before filtering for public visibility. A derived non-public member that hides a public base member by name (`private new int X`) therefore removes the public base X from contractless serialization entirely.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.GetInstanceMembers: seen.Add(member.Name) runs before the IsPublicReadable filter in CreateContractlessMembers, so the hidden public base member is never considered.
